This is user-facing for our chat flow.

We captured traces and a sample request/response for you (attached: greenridge-trace-20280922.jsonl). The errors look like "out of memory"/inference stalls interleaved with some decode errors; we also exported GPU metrics as requested (redwood-debug-gpu-metrics-20280922.csv).

This is impacting our SLOs for the week and our ops team is fielding customer reports. Can you confirm whether this correlates with the new quantization profiles or a model variant flip?

We need an immediate mitigation plan and ETA for a rollback or patch. Please escalate to engineering and ops.

Thanks,
Samantha

Subject: Analysis and proposed remediation for Greenridge (v4.2)

Rachel / Laura — quick root-cause and proposed plan below after replaying Greenridge traces and infra logs.

Summary (root cause):
- We observed that the v4.2 release included a subtle change to the quantization profile parser that caused certain attention-kernel choices to select an alternate fused-kernel path for long prefix sequences. In combination with the customer's traffic shape (bursty QPS spikes to specific token patterns), this led to transient KV cache expansion and intermittent GPU memory pressure.
- GPU metrics show repeated allocation/free cycles and driver stalls at ~02:15-02:30 UTC that align with p95 spikes and decode timeouts. Decoding errors at the application layer were secondary to these stalls.

Impact: p95 increase (median 450ms -> 1.4s), throughput down ~25%, 5xx up ~6% for Greenridge on the v4.2 variant. Other customers with dissimilar traffic shapes are unaffected so far.

Immediate remediation options:
A) Manual route: override Greenridge to v4.1 (previous model/quant) — immediate rollback of user impact, low risk. Command: "route set --customer GR --variant v4.1 --priority forced --expires 2028-09-24T08:00:00Z"
B) Hotfix: revert the qprofile parsing change and ship a v4.2.1 patch. Requires ~4 hours validation in canary, deploy window 1h. Lower blast radius but takes longer.
C) Safety guard: deploy a runtime guard that detects KV-cache growth and forces per-request fallback to non-fused kernel for affected token patterns — quick but invasive (higher risk).

Recommended next steps:
1) Execute A immediately to stop impact to Greenridge.
2) Start B in parallel: engineer validation and canary (we've drafted a patch; attached: hotfix-patch.diff).
3) Monitor for any residual errors; keep routing rule in place until v4.2.1 validated.

Requested approvals:
- Rachel: Can you confirm we have customer sign-off to force-route to v4.1 now?
- Laura: we will need executive sign-off for an enforced override and for customer communication (we'll draft a short incident note).

I'll be on call and can push the routing change as soon as Rachel confirms.

-Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: hotfix-patch.diff
